main_text.p: rabimus. Specie vitij: Apostrophe ad Idumæos: Accusationem impiæ fiduciæ de perpetua & inuista fortuna.
main_text.head: DE VITII SPECIE QVAE est superbia cordis.
main_text.p: Hebræa habent, זָדוֹן לִבְּךָ [?] Superbia cordis seu animi tui, decipitte. Meminerimus cordis superbiā, à Deo qui cordiū scrutator est, sed per os prophetæ, redargui: eamq; tū toti Idumæorū genti, tū præcipuè magistratibus, culmisima palatia, & arces in sublimi positas, incolentibus, tribui. Etsi aut alia vitia cōmunia sunt omnib. feré gentibus, alia quarundā getiū veluti proprias sunt: superbia tamen communis est, ijs potisimū quæ logæ pacis & successuū cōmodis affuetę, sese ex tra teli iactu & aduerse fortunæ alea, positas esse putant. In harū numero olim fuit Idumæa gens, vt ex prophetarū concionib. & illius historia liquet. Testatur aut Propheta, Idumæos infeliciter felices esse, quando superbia ea turgidi sint, quæ illos decipiat. Quis enim eos felices esse credat, quæ re delectatur plurimū, quæ illos subdole circumuentos decipit? Quis sanus delectetur potu venenato, si maximè labra poculi aurea, aut mellita esse videat? page.notes: Hebrew phrase after "Hebræa habent" (Obadiah 3 style, "pride of thy heart") is copied from a faint scan; vowels and letters uncertain, marked [?]. "munitifsimas" reads as "muni" + "tifsimas" across a line end with no printed hyphen; the long s is printed as f, so written as f is avoided where unclear. The final "tifsi-" at the foot is a catchword. The top line is the end of a paragraph begun on the previous page and is treated as a continuation. Some letters in "cordiū", "tū", "mōtiū" are printed with abbreviation marks as seen.
